title: Formal quotient presentations with their coherent atlas actions
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal F$ a stack fibred in groupoids as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], $Q$ an $S$-scheme, $H$ a group, $\rho:H\to\operatorname{Aut}_S(Q)$ an action, and $f:Q\to\mathcal F$ a morphism. A coherent atlas action is a system $\theta_h:f\rho_h\simeq f$, over $S$, with $\theta_1=1$ and $\theta_{hk}=(\rho_k^*\theta_h)\theta_k$.

For an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure], an object $x\in\mathcal F(\Omega)$ and a scheme map $t:T\to\mathcal F$ over $\Omega$, membership in the formal completion along the residual gerbe of $x$ means that every geometric point of $T$ gives an object isomorphic to the scalar extension of $x$. The residual gerbe is the full substack of objects locally isomorphic to $x$.

Let $Z\subset Q$ be a specified support for a formal atlas (closed in the intended application) and let $P(T,t)$ describe the target completion. An atlas-and-arrows presentation of that completion as the quotient by $H$ means: $Z$ is $H$-stable; maps $a:T\to Q$ supported on $Z$ give objects satisfying $P$; every object satisfying $P$ lifts to such an $a$ etale locally on $T$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]; every isomorphism $fa\simeq fb$ between supported atlas maps is etale locally the inverse of $a^*\theta_h$, with $a\rho_h=b$; and this group label is unique on each nonempty test scheme. Covering sieves permit arbitrary etale local trivializations, so this is the groupoid of $H$-torsors with equivariant maps, not the groupoid of globally trivial torsors. In the Noetherian case with finitely generated ideal of definition, support on $Z$ is equivalent to locally annihilating a power of that ideal, giving the usual formal scheme. For a specified geometric point $b$ of the atlas its stabilizer is the subgroup $\{h\in H:b\rho_h=b\}$.
